maria_support: FYI customer acct_acme (acct_987) reported short 429 bursts around 13:02-13:05 UTC despite having a positive burst-credit balance. Posting header sample they captured below, and a quick repro. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria_support: ```
GET /v1/complete 200 OK
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000000
x-burst-credits: 3
x-burst-credit-refill-secs: 3600
x-concurrency-used: 18
```

deploy-bot: Note: deploy to prod-routing-group-4 at 12:58 UTC (no schema changes).

sam_sre: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) did the customer run a high-concurrency backfill or many parallel short requests? 2) can you drop the exact client-side pattern (qps + concurrency) or any request logs?

maria_support: They ran a backfill with 40 workers across ~8 hosts, each ~2-3 concurrent streams hitting completions for ~30s bursts. Repro curl we gave them:

maria_support: ```bash
for i in {1..40}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete?model=redwood-1" &
done
```

jess_eng: This rings like our smoothing/soft-cap interaction — short bursts with high concurrency can exhaust the effective per-client concurrency slot even if raw burst credits > 0. A couple of mechanics to be aware of: 1) burst credits are refilled on a coarse interval and are applied against token-level billing, but we also have a short-window concurrency smoothing that deducts a temporary "smoothing budget" based on sustained concurrency over ~1-3m windows. 2) If many workers ramp in simultaneously the concurrency gate can transiently deny requests while the smoothing budget recalculates.

jess_eng: TL;DR: positive x-burst-credits doesn't strictly guarantee zero 429s when concurrency spikes and smoothing kicks in.

sam_sre: Can you capture rate-limiter events (rl:burst_drain, rl:concurrency_drop) for acct_987 between 13:00-13:10? If you paste the internal event lines I can confirm the throttle reason. Also check client-side headers: x-rw-blocked-reason or x-rw-smoothing-state if present.

maria_support: Pasting a snippet from customer logs (sanitized):

maria_support: ```
[13:02:14] rl_event: acct=acct_987 ev=burst_drain credits_before=3 credits_after=0 reason=concurrency_spike
[13:02:15] request_rejected status=429 route=/v1/complete details="concurrency soft-cap hit"
[13:03:02] rl_event: smoothing_decay acct=acct_987 decay_percent=20
[13:04:30] rl_event: credits_refill acct=acct_987 amount=1
```

jess_eng: Perfect — that confirms the smoothing budget being drained faster than credits were refilled. Two mitigation paths: short-term (what we should tell customer now) and medium-term (platform changes).

jess_eng: Short-term recommendations: 1) reduce parallelism (go from 40 -> 8 workers) or add jitter/startup ramps; 2) add client-side exponential backoff on 429s (retry-after awareness); 3) if eligible, temporarily bump their reserved capacity / request a transient quota increase. Example backoff: `sleep_time = base * (1.5 ** retries) + jitter`.

elena_csm: I'll tell the customer to throttle their backfill and give them a config snippet. Also offering a temporary reserved pool for the job window if legal approves.

sam_sre: For platform follow-up: we should consider exposing a clearer header that reports smoothing budget vs burst credits (eg `x-rw-smoothing-remaining`) so customers can distinguish which cap fired. Also add an internal alert when rl:burst_drain events spike for an account.

jess_eng: Agreed. I'll open a small ticket to: 1) add smoothing metrics to the per-account dashboard, 2) consider making refill granularity finer (but need to simulate cost impact), 3) add a telemetry field in headers.

maria_support: I told the customer to stagger workers and try the backoff snippet; they confirmed reduced 429s after throttling. Leaving this thread for tracking — will update if they opt for reserved capacity. :thumbsup:

jess_eng: Thanks all — marking for follow-up. If you can grab the rl_event lines for 13:00-13:10 and drop them into the ticket, that's the last piece I need.
